threads.body: `randomVet()` still selects its last name from `adj`, which includes `Freakin' awesome`; that value violates the pinned image's [surname pattern](https://github.com/spring-petclinic/spring-petclinic-rest/blob/220f4ba8e92cec9ad1faa03324723a3e9da63d95/src/main/resources/openapi.yml#L2230-L2236). When selected, POST `/vets` returns HTTP 400 and the new zero-failure k6 thresholds fail the benchmark run. Select the last name from `surnames`, as `randomOwner()` already does.

replies.body: Fixed in 344f476bd93bbe35318d46763a0191ca9fa1c648. `randomVet()` now selects from `surnames`, and a deterministic generator regression test covers the invalid-surname case. The zero-failure k6 thresholds remain unchanged.

threads.body: [Simplification] The three new JFR command checks repeat the same steps: run the command, check the exit code, and throw an `IllegalStateException` with the result. A small private helper could replace all three and keep the context-specific messages. For example: `private static void execChecked(GenericContainer<?> container, String errorMessage, String... command)`. Call it from `startRecording` and from the warmup start and stop calls in `doWarmupPhase`.

Nothing runs this test: no Gradle task, workflow or README step calls `k6 run k6/names-test.js`. A regression in `names.js` would therefore go unnoticed. Either add it to a build or CI step (for example, a k6 run before `basic.js`) or document how to run it. It also gets copied into the k6 container's `/app`, since `K6Container` copies the whole `./k6` directory.
